newsitem.title: INDIA: CHRONOLOGY - Winning party in India Punjab never completed term.
newsitem.headline: CHRONOLOGY - Winning party in India Punjab never completed term.

text.p: The pro-Sikh Akali Dal party of India's northern state of Punjab, which won a thumping victory in Friday's local assembly elections, has yet to complete a five-year term in three decades.
The Akali Dal contested the polls in a rare alliance with the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
Akali leaders blame hostility from the Congress party, which has ruled Punjab for most of the period since independence from Britain in 1947, for not allowing their previous governments to last.
The Akali Dal's fortunes were linked with the division of Punjab, at first in 1947, when the state's western portions went to Pakistan following the partition of British-ruled India.

India split the rest of the predominantly Hindu region in 1966 into the Hindi-speaking states of Haryana and Himachal Pradesh and the Punjabi-speaking Punjab, giving the Sikhs a religious majority in the state.
The state capital of Chandigarh, shared by Haryana and Punjab, was also carved out from agriculture-rich Punjab.
Following is a chronology of the state's governments showing the year of taking power, chief ministers and their party:
1947 August Gopi Chand Bhargava Congress party
1949 April Bhim Sen Sachar Congress party
1949 Oct Gopi Chand Bhargava Congress party
1951 June President's rule
1952 April Bhim Sen Sachar Congress party
1956 January Pratap S. Kairon Congress party
1964 June Gopi Chand Bhargava Congress party
1964 July Ram Kishan Congress party
1966 July President's rule
1966 Nov Giani Gurmukh Singh Congress party
1966 Nov Division of Punjab, giving Sikhs a majority
1967 March Gurnam Singh Akali Dal
1967 Nov Lachman Singh Gill Akali Dal
1968 Aug President's rule
1969 Feb Gurnam Singh Akali Dal
1970 March Prakash Singh Badal Akali Dal
1972 March Giani Zail Singh Congress party
1977 June Prakash Singh Badal Akali Dal
1980 Feb President's rule
1980 July Darbara Singh Congress party
1983 Oct President's rule
1985 Sept Surjit Singh Barnala Akali Dal
1987 May President's rule
1992 Feb Beant Singh Congress party
1995 August H.S. Brar Congress party
1996 Nov Rajinder Kaur Bhattal Congress party
1997 Feb Prakash Singh Badal (designate)Akali Dal
